 Belmont businesses prepare for rise in minimum wage
 Sahana Patel , Staff Writer 
 • 
 November 18, 2026 
 A set of doors opens to Hassett Ace Hardware in the Carlmont Village Shopping Center, one of the many businesses in Belmont whose wages may change following the minimum wage increase in 2027. “As time goes on, people need more money just to get by, even if it’s just a small change,” said Andrea Negrete, a Carlmont senior who works at United Studios of Self Defense, a studio located in the same area. 
 The minimum wage in Belmont, California, will rise in January 2027 from $18.95 to $19.60, a 3.43% increase from 2026. 
 The minimum wage in Belmont is rising in accordance with the Consumer Price Index, which measures changes in the prices consumers pay for goods and services. 
 The goal of Belmont’s minimum wage rise is to offset living costs, especially on the San Francisco Peninsula, where the cost of living is much higher compared to other parts of the country.  However, the increase presents a balancing act for businesses throughout Belmont. 
 Some express concerns about the financial impact of the increase, including Pooja Khanna, owner of the after-school math and reading enrichment program Kumon’s Belmont location.
 “The economy is already not doing that great. My business is already impacted, and my profitability will go down,” Khanna said. 
 Despite these concerns, Khanna said that minimum wage protections are important for employees, helping them manage costs and ensuring fair compensation. 
 “It’s important if you’re taking someone’s service. You should pay them properly based on their skills,” Khanna said. 
 Andrea Negrete, a Carlmont senior who works at the United Studios of Self Defense in Belmont, noted the value of minimum-wage protections for working students.  
 “Minimum wage is important because it sets a baseline. If there wasn’t a minimum wage, many employers would take advantage,” Negrete said. 
 https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/30941552/visualisation.json?ref=embed-script 
 Minimum wage increases also affect businesses differently based on their size. Larger businesses tend to have greater financial flexibility to accommodate labor costs, while smaller businesses may feel effects immediately.  
 “Big companies have large margins. Because it’s a small business, the income is not as high. I can see changes in my expenses right away,” Khanna said. 
 Khanna also said there is a possibility of reducing her workforce and the additional responsibilities she would have to take on as a result. 
 “For a small business, the owner will be impacted. If I can’t employ employees, I will have to work much harder. It will impact my lifestyle, and my work-life balance,” Khanna said. 
 William Kaldenbaugh, a Carlmont senior and a member of the Distributive Education Clubs of America, also discussed how the increase could affect businesses of different sizes. 
 “Smaller businesses might be more affected because they don’t have as many employees, so each employee plays a bigger role in the operations of the business,” Kaldenbaugh said. 
 Beyond its effects on businesses, the minimum wage increase could also benefit employees, especially students working to save for future expenses.  
 “College is also getting more expensive. A lot of teenagers are getting part-time jobs because they’re saving for college,” Negrete said. 
 https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/30927079/visualisation.json?ref=embed-script 
 Kaldenbaugh also talked about the rising cost of living in the Bay Area and how higher wages could help employees manage everyday expenses.  
 “Here in the Bay Area, it’s really expensive to live, compared to the rest of the country,” Kaldenbaugh said. “It would make it a lot easier for people to live their lives without worrying about rent or being able to put food on the table.”
